neighbours.label: a noun right after a participle adjective (setting sun, smashed windows, published articles): fires on the noun the participle modifies
fire: Out on the lake we watched the rising moon over the pines.
Every morning the janitor swept up broken bottles in the alley.
We stood on the deck and listened to the crashing waves below.
The archive keeps signed letters from the war years.
Tourists photographed the frozen waterfall all winter.
In the back room he found stolen paintings wrapped in sheets.
Outside the camp the barking dogs kept everyone awake.
After the storm, fallen trees blocked the county road.
quiet: Out on the lake we watched the full moon over the pines.
Every morning the janitor swept up green bottles in the alley.
We stood on the deck and listened to the big waves below.
The archive keeps old letters from the war years.
Tourists photographed the tall waterfall all winter.
In the back room he found large paintings wrapped in sheets.
Outside the camp the hungry dogs kept everyone awake.
After the storm, huge trees blocked the county road.

notes: Probes: setting sun 0.94, smashed windows 1.00, published articles 0.97, melting ice 0.33; the same nouns without the participle 0.01. Near misses keep an ordinary adjective, so the test separates participle from any adjective.
